name: Gradient Boosting
description: Gradient Boosting is a machine learning technique for regression and classification problems that produces a prediction model in the form of an ensemble of weak prediction models, typically decision trees. It builds models sequentially, with each new tree correcting errors made by previous trees.
how_it_works: The algorithm starts with a simple model and iteratively adds weak learners (typically shallow decision trees). Each new tree is trained to predict the negative gradient (pseudo-residuals) of the loss function with respect to the current ensemble predictions. A learning rate shrinks each tree's contribution to prevent overfitting.

complexity.time: O(n * log(n) * d * T) where n=samples, d=features, T=trees
complexity.space: O(n + T * nodes_per_tree) for data and model storage

key_parameters: min_child_weight: minimum sum of instance weight in leaf
subsample: fraction of samples used per tree
colsample_bytree: fraction of features per tree
pseudocode_or_diagram_description: Initialize F_0(x) = argmin_gamma sum L(y_i, gamma). For m=1 to M: compute pseudo-residuals r_im = -[dL(y_i, F(x_i))/dF(x_i)] for all i. Fit tree h_m(x) to residuals. Find optimal step size rho_m via line search. Update: F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + learning_rate * rho_m * h_m(x). Final model F_M(x) is the ensemble.
